summary: Recent testimony (2013) of an old observation (1971). Observation lasting approximately one minute of the straight and silent passage of a circular object with two rows of "portholes" rotating on itself: lack of information.
description: On November 2, 1971, between approximately 7:10 and 7:40 PM, the witness (then six and a half years old) was returning home from sports practice. A friend alerted him to the presence of an object in the sky. Intrigued, the witness observed a circular object shaped like a saucer with two rows of windows. This object appeared to rotate on its axis while moving at low altitude without making any noise. The object was directly above the street the witness was about to take to get home. However, upon reaching an intersection, the child took his eyes off the UFO: the UFO continued on its straight path. Unfortunately, once home, the child never saw the object in the sky again. Only one witness statement was collected (see the investigation report). The hypothesis of a lost balloon would largely fit the description (straight trajectory, silence, low altitude, duration of the observation, etc.), but cannot be validated as the search failed to find a balloon with the characteristics described by the witness (windows, color, size, etc.). The color change noted at the end of the observation also weakens this hypothesis. The testimony, rich in detail, is surprising given the young age of the witness. Only one of the two known witnesses testified to GEIPAN and was interviewed. The consistency of the evidence is compromised by the long delay after the observation (45 years), which could alter the memory, and also by the fact that only one of the two witnesses recorded the event. The evidence is too weak to validate the strange and unexplained nature of the observation. For example, it is not possible to verify certain important details, and it is not possible to rule out the possibility of a lost child's balloon with strong evidence. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: late testimony unusable due to lack of reliable information
